Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits the ZINB model: with probability \(\pi_i\) an observation is a structural zero, otherwise it follows an NB(\(\mu_i\), \(\theta\)) distribution, with \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{logit}\, \pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\). The likelihood is maximized by the EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability \(\tau_i\) of being a structural zero. The zero-part M-step is a logistic regression with fractional response \(\tau_i\) fitted by IRLS, and the count-part M-step is the NB fit of nbreg() with prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\). No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before the bar, zero-model covariates after it. If there is no |, the same covariates are used in both parts. An offset() term in the count part is allowed.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional numeric offset for the count model, evaluated in data.

control

A list of control settings from zinbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "zinbreg", a list with components including coefficients (a list with elements count and zero), vcov (for count_*, zero_* and Log(theta)), theta, se.theta, logtheta, se.logtheta, loglik, df, iter, converged, loglik.path, fitted.values, mu, pi, tau, y and call.

Details

Standard errors come from the inverse of the observed information matrix of the observed-data log-likelihood with respect to \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\), computed from the analytic Hessian.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 400
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
pz <- plogis(-1 + 0.8 * d$z)
d$y <- ifelse(runif(n) < pz, 0, rnbinom(n, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x), size = 2))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
fit$coefficients
#> $count
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   1.0657977   0.4689358 
#> 
#> $zero
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -1.1858462   0.9021801 
#> 
fit$theta
#> [1] 1.523283
